claims.text: Optimizing spray distance and powder feed rate with the HVAF-i7 torch will increase FeCoNiCrAl particle velocity.
An effective spray-distance range is 300–350 mm.
An effective powder-feed-rate range is 20–30 g/min.
The proposed operating conditions produce particle velocities of 500–600 m/s.
Increasing particle velocity increases particle kinetic energy.
Higher particle velocity and kinetic energy improve particle flattening.
Higher particle velocity increases deposition efficiency.
Improved particle flattening and deposition efficiency increase coating thickness.
The optimized conditions will increase coating thickness by 20–30% relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock HVAF-i7 baseline.
The optimized conditions will maintain coating integrity.
The optimized conditions will maintain minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
The intervention remains applicable to deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
The magnitude of the thickness increase may depend on operating conditions and material properties.

contradictions.description: A 300–350 mm nozzle-to-substrate spray distance appears geometrically incompatible with coating the wall of a 120 mm internal diameter, for which the available radial stand-off is at most about 60 mm unless a different spray geometry is specified.

The prediction requires coating integrity and oxidation performance to be maintained, whereas the falsification rule requires coating 'properties' to be significantly improved. Maintenance and significant improvement are different criteria.
